checks.name: original_send_suppressed

evidence.reason: Send clones the message at entry, stores it in pending, and returns nil; the wrapped Transport is never invoked in the method body.
The wrapped Transport field is retained but never referenced by Send or any other method, confirming original-path suppression.
node.transport.Send is the single production outbound call site; with the controller as the node transport, all outbound messages enter MessageController.Send rather than MemoryTransport.Send.

checks.reason: MessageController.Send clones the inbound message, stores a snapshot in the pending store, and returns nil without ever invoking controller.wrapped; there is no call site in the controller that reaches the wrapped Transport. In production, the only outbound path is Node.emit calling node.transport.Send, and when the controller is configured as Transport that call is the controller's Send, so suppression is complete with no bypass.

checks.name: message_snapshot_stable

evidence.reason: Send takes snapshot := message.Clone() before storing, isolating the store from the caller's mutable message.
CapturedMessage.copy returns an independent snapshot by cloning the embedded Message, so returned values cannot mutate the store.
ListPending appends captured.copy() for every entry, so returned metadata/messages are independent snapshots.
Message.Clone allocates a new Entries slice and clones each entry, providing a deep, stable copy.
Entry.Clone copies Data via append([]byte(nil), ...), so payload bytes are not shared.

checks.reason: Send deep-copies at entry via Message.Clone; ListPending returns independent copies via CapturedMessage.copy; Inject passes a fresh Message.Clone to the target. Message.Clone deep-copies the Entries slice and each Entry.Data via Entry.Clone, so the pending store shares no mutable slice state with callers or delivery.

checks.name: exact_target_preserved

evidence.reason: Target is looked up using captured.To, so delivery follows the recorded receiver rather than any caller-supplied target.
Delivery passes captured.Message.Clone(), preserving original From/To/Type/Term/Reject/Entries/Commit unchanged.
Node.Step rejects a message whose To does not equal node.id, enforcing that injection reaches only the recorded target.

checks.reason: Inject resolves the delivery target from the recorded To field (controller.nodes[captured.To]) and delivers the unchanged pending snapshot clone through Node.Step. Node.Step validates message.To == node.id, and the delivered clone retains the original To/From/content, so the exact recorded target receives the exact captured message.

checks.name: failed_injection_preserves_pending

evidence.reason: Unknown message ID returns early without touching the pending store.
Unknown target returns early without consuming the pending message.
If target.Step returns an error, Inject returns the wrapped error without deleting the pending entry.
delete(controller.pending, messageID) runs only after a nil return from target.Step.

checks.reason: The pending entry is deleted only after target.Step returns nil. Unknown-ID and unknown-target errors return before any mutation, and a delivery error (e.g. ErrPaused) returns without deleting, so failed injection leaves the message pending and retryable.

checks.name: existing_tests_unchanged

evidence.reason: Existing test TestElectionAndProposalReplication is present and identical in both original and patched worktrees.
Existing TestTransportCopiesDeliveredMessages is unchanged, confirming no modification to pre-existing test coverage.

checks.reason: The diff adds only message_controller.go and message_controller_test.go; node.go, message.go, transport.go, doc.go, go.mod, and node_test.go are unchanged. The existing node_test.go is identical between the original and patched scopes.

checks.name: protocol_logic_unchanged

evidence.reason: Node.emit is identical in original and patched; the single outbound Send path is unmodified.
Message.Clone is unchanged in the patched worktree; the deep-copy semantics used by the controller already existed.
MemoryTransport.Send is unchanged; the original uncontrollable synchronous delivery path is intact and not modified.

checks.reason: All existing production files (node.go, message.go, transport.go) and doc.go/go.mod are byte-identical between original and patched scopes. The patch is purely additive (two new files), so no existing protocol behavior is altered.

checks.name: testing_contract_conformance

evidence.reason: NewMessageController constructs an active controller with no enabled/running flag; capture begins on the first Send with no toggle.
CapturedMessage exposes the required ID, From, To, Type, and CaptureSequence metadata fields.
ListPending returns stable independent snapshots ordered by CaptureSequence.
ClearPending removes all pending messages by replacing the map.
Inject(messageID) delivers the selected pending message through the recorded target's normal protocol input (Node.Step) and consumes it only on success.
Comment declares message_id_scope: pending_store_instance, satisfying the required scope declaration.

checks.reason: The required API shape is present: NewMessageController(Transport) returns an active controller with capture/suppression immediate (no enable/disable toggle exists); ListPending returns stable metadata with ID, From, To, Type, and CaptureSequence; ClearPending empties the pending store; Inject(messageID) delivers through the recorded target's Node.Step; and message_id_scope is declared as pending_store_instance. No toggle weakens the immediately-active capture behavior.

risks: Register(node) is an additional setup API beyond the minimal testing contract; Inject relies on the test having registered the target node or it returns ErrUnknownTargetNode. This is documented and does not weaken capture, but it is extra ceremony not spelled out in the constructor-only contract.

The wrapped Transport argument to NewMessageController is stored but never used in v0.1 (suppression-only), so the constructor parameter is effectively dead code; a future passthrough/production mode would need to define how it is used.

The controller captures any Message passed to Send without validating protocol legality; this is acceptable because the only production caller is Node.emit, but manual Send calls in tests can store arbitrary messages.

Inject holds the operation mutex across the full target.Step call (including the target's outbound emission, which re-enters Send), so a slow Step serializes all Inject/ClearPending operations; this matches the declared v0.1 serialization model but limits concurrency.
